author: Syme
text_post: RE: The Right to be Offensive. By current legal system I assume you mean the system in the United States. If so, then you should be aware that contrary to the First Amendment, there are definite limits to free speech that go way beyond threats and contractual agreements. For example there are laws against libel and slander, which are a definite violation of the right to free expression. The right to free expression must contain the right to lie. Otherwise, any court can quite simply abridge free speech because ultimately it's a judge and/or a jury who decide what counts as true or false in conentious cases. The idea of protecting someone's reputation is also nonsense. No one owns his reputation. It exists solely in the minds of other people. Being protected against loss of reputation essentially means controlling the minds of other people. These laws are also highly dangerous because they effectively make contentious free speech a privilege of the rich. Poorer people cannot afford to hire a lawyer to sue for defamation or libel. And since these laws do exist, the public is more inclined to believe statements made without sufficient evidence. Moreover, these laws can be used to silence people who cannot afford lengthy legal procedures.

text_post: RE: The Right to be Offensive. Consider it this way. The old adage "sticks and stones may break my bones but words can never hurt me." Unpleasant words can be unpleasant, and a person tends to remember them with a suitably emotional response, but they do not cause physical harm. Even threats of violence, while filling a person with fear and reducing their quality of life, causes no physical harm. Even the mental harm suffered is more the choice of the hearer than of the speaker. However, how do you stop people from speaking? With, to follow the adage, sticks and stones. Only violence can prevent people from opening their mouths, or at the very least the threat of violence if they do so. If someone says something offensive then the people who hear it are free to express their opinion of those words, publicly shun the person, or simply avoid them. Anything beyond that is using sticks and stones to harm someone for words, and violates the non-aggression principle.
